canonical_attributes.listing.title: American Job Centers Network
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The American Job Center network offers free help to job seekers for certain career and employment-related needs. There are nearly 2,400 American Job Centers (or AJCs) across the U.S. Published requirements: AJCs help people search for jobs, find training, answer other employment questions, and more. You may also get free computer access if you need it. Visit CareerOneStop to find information and resources. Application or referral: For many AJC services, there is nothing you need to apply for. Many are self-service. You may only need to apply for certain special services. Contact your local center for details. Page last updated: 03/10/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: Assistance for Families
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The Administration for Children & Families (ACF) helps provide programs and funding for families with low income. We have two programs that may be able to help you after a disaster. Published requirements: Your family must have low income to qualify. Application or referral: Below are the two programs we offer. Visit the program pages to get more details on how to apply. Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) This program can help if your family has low income and has children. It offers income support and services to help you gain financial security and stability. Visit Help for Families to get application information for your state, territory, or tribe. find information for your area and learn how to apply. Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) This program may help if you have low income and need help with the following: Home energy bills, weatherization, and minor energy-related home repairs. Read the LIHEAP Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for details. Page last updated: 03/24/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: Bureau of Indian Affairs Financial Assistance and Social Services (FASS)
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Financial Assistance and Social Services (FASS) program offers five types of financial assistance to American Indians or Alaska Natives: General Assistance Child Assistance Non-medical Institutional or Custodial Care of Adults Burial Assistance Emergency Assistance Visit the Direct Assistance (Financial Assistance & Social Services) page to learn more about these services and how to apply. Published requirements: You must meet all of the conditions below to qualify: Be an enrolled member of a federally recognized American Indian or Alaska Native tribe. Prove you are not able to pay for the needs of food, clothing, shelter, and utilities. Live in or near an approved service area. Apply for all other federal, state, tribal, county, and local programs you may qualify for. Confirm you don’t get any other similar assistance. Application or referral: You can apply at the nearest BIA-operated or tribal social service provider. Contact your local BIA regional office to find one near you. Page last updated: 03/23/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: Convert Your Federal Benefit Check
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: Do you get federal benefit payments by paper check? If so, you must now switch to electronic payments. You may choose from two payment options: Direct Deposit – Automatically deposit your money directly into your checking or savings account. Direct Express® Debit MasterCard® – Get a prepaid debit card you can use just like other debit cards and get cash. Read Before You Begin Enrollment to learn more about direct deposit. You may also visit the Direct Express card page to learn about the card’s features and fees. Published requirements: You can switch to direct deposit from any of the agencies below: Social Security Administration (SSA) Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Veterans Affairs (VA) (Compensation, pension, and some education payments) Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Application or referral: Use one of the options below to sign up for direct deposit: Visit the GoDirect website. Call 1-877-874-6347. Complete application to enroll by mail . To sign up for the Direct Express card, call 1-800-333-1795. We will send your enrollment information directly to the agencies. Page last updated: 03/30/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: Disaster Assistance and Emergency Relief Program for Individuals and Businesses
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: Did a federally declared disaster affect you? If so, you may get extra time to file and pay your current tax returns and payments. Visit the IRS news from around the nation page. Click on your state to see a list of returns and payments that qualify under this program. Published requirements: If you meet both of the conditions below, you don’t need to contact the IRS to get the extra time. It is automatic. You must live in a county the IRS identified for disaster tax relief. Your address on file must be up to date. Application or referral: If any of the conditions below apply to you, please call IRS Special Services at 1-866-562-5227. You live in a federally declared disaster area and – Your address is not up to date. You have other tax-related hardships. You are not able to make your installment payments on back-due taxes. canonical_attributes.listing.title: FEMA Disaster Recovery Center (DRC) / DRC Locator
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: After a disaster, FEMA works with the state, Tribal Nation, or territory to open Disaster Recovery Centers (DRCs) in or near affected communities. The centers can help you apply for FEMA assistance and offer other information and resources to help with your recovery. You may also visit to ask questions about your case. DRCs are set up in facilities and mobile offices for all survivors to access. The DRC Locator shows the hours, services, and locations of centers near you. Published requirements: DRCs are open to anyone who wants to come in. There are no program requirements to visit. Application or referral: You don’t have to apply for anything to visit a DRC. We’re here to help. Page last updated: 08/05/2025.

canonical_attributes.listing.title: FEMA Individuals and Households Program (IHP)
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: FEMA's Individuals and Households Program may provide money and limited direct housing services to help you after a disaster. If you have damage to your home, you needed to move, or you have other serious needs due to a presidentially declared disaster, the program may be able to help. Published requirements: You can get help from this program if you meet all of the conditions below: You are a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national, or qualified alien. FEMA can confirm your identity. Your costs or needs are caused by a presidentially declared disaster. Your insurance or other assistance sources don’t cover your costs or needs. Most forms of assistance are limited to losses related to your primary home. Visit the Individuals and Households Program page to learn more. Application or referral: There are several ways you can apply: Start an application online. Call FEMA’s Helpline at 1-800-621-3362 . Visit a Disaster Recovery Center (DRC). You can use the DRC Locator to find a center near you. Page last updated: 12/05/2025. Links published on the directory page (not independently assessed): Individuals and Households Program — https://www.fema.gov/assistance/individual/library#fact-sheets; Start an application online. — https://www.disasterassistance.gov/DAC-RI/en/assessment/captcha; DRC Locator — https://egateway.fema.gov/ESF6/DRCLocator

canonical_attributes.listing.title: HUD Housing Assistance Programs
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) funds two housing assistance programs. These programs may be able to help you find a new place to live after a disaster. The programs can provide safe, affordable housing for those who qualify. Your local Public Housing Agency (PHA) manages both programs. Visit the program pages to learn more. Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) This program helps you by paying part of your rent. We do this through a subsidy paid directly to your landlord. Public Housing This program offers decent, safe housing at rent you can afford. Published requirements: If you are a family with low-income, an older adult, or a person with a disability, you may qualify. Your local PHA will decide if you do. Application or referral: Apply through your local PHA. Find your local Public Housing Agency (PHA) to learn more about the programs or to apply. Page last updated: 03/26/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: HUD Mortgage Insurance Programs for Disaster Recovery
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) offers two mortgage insurance programs that can help homeowners after a disaster. The programs also offer options for those who want to buy a home. Visit the program pages to get more details: Mortgage Insurance for Disaster Victims Section 203(h) This program makes it easier for you to get a mortgage after a disaster. It can help you buy a home or rebuild your destroyed or damaged primary home. To rebuild, the home must be in a presidentially declared disaster area. Section 203(k) Rehabilitation Mortgage Insurance This program is for both homeowners and those who want to buy a home. You can get a mortgage that helps you buy or refinance a home and covers the cost to repair it. Published requirements: Contact an FHA-approved lender or a HUD-certified housing counselor to find out if you qualify. Application or referral: Find and contact a HUD-approved housing counseling agency to learn more about these programs and get help to apply. You can also call 1-800-569-4287 . canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. It pays back certain expenses for victims of terrorism outside of the U.S. Your incident must appear on the Terrorist Incident Designation List to apply. If it is not on the list, our staff will request to add it. You must also have suffered direct physical or emotional injury or death due to the act of terrorism. A family member or legal agent may apply for a victim who is a minor, unable to apply for themselves, or killed. Application or referral: Go to the Forms and Checklists page on the ITVERP website for more details and to apply. Page last updated: 03/24/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: Domestic violence can happen in any relationship. It can happen in families, dating, and even in other relationships. We offer two safe, private call-in hotlines for victims of domestic violence. These hotlines are available 24 hours a day, every day. The National Domestic Violence Hotline (“The Hotline”) provides access to many free, private services and support. They are available for both adult and youth victims of domestic violence, their family members, and to the public. Interpreters are available by phone to help in over 200 languages. StrongHearts Native Helpline is also an anonymous helpline for American Indian and Alaska Native victims of domestic and sexual violence. This line offers access to culturally appropriate support and services. Published requirements: The Hotline and StrongHearts Native Helpline calls and services are free. Application or referral: You don’t need to apply for anything. Page last updated: 03/24/2026. canonical_attributes.listing.title: National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
canonical_attributes.listing.summary: DisasterAssistance.gov lists this assistance/resource entry. Description: The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) allows homeowners, business owners, and renters in communities that participate in the program to buy government-backed flood insurance. This insurance helps cover repairs for flood damage to buildings and contents. For many forms of disaster assistance you must have and keep flood insurance. Published requirements: Your community must participate in NFIP for you to be covered by this program. You can use FEMA's Community Status Book to search for your community. Visit the NFIP page for details. Application or referral: Call or visit the pages below to learn more about your flood risk and flood insurance options. Visit the U.S. Department of Labor's State Unemployment Insurance Benefits page to learn more about benefits. Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) may provide short-term benefits to people who lost or had their job or self-employment stopped because of a disaster. Your state will announce if DUA is available. If you don’t qualify for regular UI, and DUA is available in your state, you might qualify for DUA. Visit the DUA page to learn more. Application or referral: Contact your state's UI agency to file a claim when you can’t work anymore. Try to file as soon as you can. Use the CareerOneStop Unemployment Benefits Finder to find your state's agency. If you evacuated or moved to another state, file a claim in the state where the disaster happened.
